report.policy_wording_name: Arogya Sanjeevani Policy, Niva Bupa Health Insurance Co. Ltd. (UIN NBHHLIP27056V042627)
report.headline: Ask your insurer to justify ₹60,000 of deductions
report.summary: ₹60,000 across 1 deduction needs the insurer to show its basis before you can judge it. ₹8,000 (1 item) is part of room or procedure charges. The deduction is correct, but you can ask the hospital to waive it.

deduction_findings.insurer_reason: Reasonable & customary charges - surgeon fee restricted to Rs 60,000 as per prevailing rates in the locality
deduction_findings.explanation: The policy only pays what other hospitals or doctors in the same area would charge, but the letter gives no comparison or clause. Ask the insurer in writing for the local rates it used. For a network hospital, also ask whether the fee matches the tariff the insurer agreed with that hospital. If they can't show comparable rates, escalate.

deduction_findings.insurer_reason: Subsumed into procedure charges - List III
deduction_findings.explanation: "Arthroscopy Instrument Charges" is listed as "Arthroscopy and endoscopy instruments", which is in List III of your policy's Annexure-A: it counts as part of the procedure charges, so it isn't paid as a separate line. Because this was cashless at a network hospital, you can ask the hospital to absorb it. That's a request, not a legal right.
"Hinged Knee Brace (Long)" is listed as "Knee braces (long/ short/ hinged)", which is in List I of your policy's Annexure-A (not covered). This deduction is correct.

deduction_findings.insurer_reason: Road ambulance restricted to policy limit of Rs 2,000
deduction_findings.explanation: Road ambulance is covered up to ₹2,000 per hospitalisation, so ₹1,000 of the ₹3,000 bill is correctly cut.

check_findings.issue: Deduction letter does not cite policy clauses
check_findings.explanation: 1 deduction only says things like "Reasonable & customary charges - surgeon fee restricted to Rs 60,000 as per prevailing rates in the locality". When a claim is partly disallowed, the insurer must refer to the specific terms of the policy. Ask it to name the clause for each.
The 5% co-pay (₹9,090) was correctly applied to the admissible amount after deductions (₹1,81,800).
₹5,000/day doesn't exceed the eligible ₹5,000/day, so no proportionate deduction applies.
Specific waiting periods don't apply to treatment needed because of an accident, and the policy is 9 months old, so the 30-day wait is over.
This exclusion only applies to people taking part as professionals. A recreational sports injury isn't excluded, which is useful if the insurer raises it later.

similar_cases.forum: State Commission Gujarat (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Gujarat State, Ahmedabad)
similar_cases.insurer_reason: A multifocal lens primarily has a cosmetic benefit of eliminating spectacles; cost of spectacles, surgery for correction of vision and cosmetic treatment are excluded (clauses 4.6(b), 4.7), and only medically necessary, reasonable and customary expenses are payable (clauses 3.22, 3.33).
similar_cases.reasoning: The Commission held the procedure was a cataract surgery, not a cosmetic one, and the insurer produced no contrary evidence; the spectacles/contact lens exclusion concerns external aids, not an implanted lens. The policy set no limit on cataract charges or type of lens, so the insurer could not override the treating doctor's choice of implant or use the reasonable & customary clause to restrict it. The full Rs 82,000 was awarded with 8% interest from the date of complaint.

similar_cases.insurer_reason: Surgeon's fee restricted under the Reasonable & Customary clause 2.37; excess room rent and proportionate deduction under clause 3.2; C-arm charges included in OT; dressing included in nursing; OT replacement medicines without break-up; non-medical items not payable.
similar_cases.reasoning: The Forum upheld the room-rent cap and proportionate deduction under clause 3.2 (which exempts only medicines) and the non-medical deductions. It allowed C-arm (Rs 16,000), dressing (Rs 3,500) and OT replacement (Rs 10,900) as genuinely billed. On the surgeon's fee, it held the insurer may apply the reasonable & customary clause by comparing prevailing charges in the area even without a specific cap, but to strike a balance allowed half (Rs 40,750) of the Rs 81,500 deducted.

similar_cases.insurer_reason: Covid-19 has no established protocol or standardised costs, so the claim was settled at the General Insurance Council's schedule of Covid treatment rates: Rs 59,550 deducted as in excess of GIC rates, plus Rs 3,098 for non-medical items (masks, caps, sheets) and Rs 300 miscellaneous charges.
similar_cases.reasoning: The Forum observed that the GI Council tariff was never circulated to policyholders or disclosed at claim intimation, had not been reviewed as expected and did not match actual hospital charges. As per IRDAI guidelines Covid claims must be assessed under each policy's terms; this policy had no head-wise ceilings and the insurer raised no specific objection on the reasonableness of the bill. Only the non-payable items (Rs 3,098) and miscellaneous charges (Rs 300) were upheld and the balance Rs 1,16,203 was awarded.

similar_cases.insurer_reason: Reasonable and customary charges (clause 3.29): comparable Mumbai hospitals charged Rs 18,000-30,000 for cataract surgery; package rates are negotiated with network (PPN) hospitals; for non-PPN reimbursement claims only the cost of a monofocal lens is payable; the insured should act as if uninsured when agreeing to rates.
similar_cases.reasoning: The Forum held that PPN rates are negotiated between the insurer/TPA and specific hospitals and cannot be used as the benchmark for a non-network hospital. The policy did not require treatment at a PPN hospital, had no cap on cataract surgery and did not restrict cover to a monofocal lens, and the expenses were not unreasonable. The balance of Rs 18,935 was ordered to be paid, less non-medical expenses if any.

escalation.title: Write to the insurer's grievance officer
escalation.action: Send the complaint letter ClaimBack drafts, listing each disputed amount and the clause or rule behind it. Keep proof of sending.
escalation.deadline_note: The insurer must acknowledge immediately and resolve it within 14 days, by 01 Oct 2026.

escalation.title: Register it on Bima Bharosa
escalation.action: Also log the complaint on IRDAI's Bima Bharosa portal (bimabharosa.irdai.gov.in) so it's tracked.
escalation.deadline_note: Optional, but it puts the complaint on IRDAI's record.

escalation.title: Go to the Insurance Ombudsman, Bengaluru
escalation.action: If the insurer rejects your complaint, doesn't reply, or replies unsatisfactorily, file with the Ombudsman online at cioins.co.in. It's free.
escalation.deadline_note: Possible after 30 days without a satisfactory reply. File within 1 year of the insurer's reply. Claims up to Rs 50 lakh.

escalation.title: Consumer commission (last resort)
escalation.action: If the Ombudsman route doesn't work for you, a district consumer commission can hear the dispute. You can't pursue both for the same dispute.
escalation.deadline_note: General information only; consider advice before filing.

NIVA-AS-3.29-MEDICAL-EXPENSES.title: Medical expenses limited to locality rates (reasonable & customary basis)
NIVA-AS-3.29-MEDICAL-EXPENSES.quote: Medical Expenses means those expenses that an insured person has necessarily and actually incurred for medical treatment on account of illness or accident on the advice of a medical practitioner, as long as these are no more than would have been payable if the insured person had not been insured and no more than other hospitals or doctors in the same locality would have charged for the same medical treatment.
NIVA-AS-3.29-MEDICAL-EXPENSES.source: Arogya Sanjeevani Policy, Niva Bupa Health Insurance Co. Ltd.

NIVA-AS-4.1-ROOM.title: Room rent and ICU limits
NIVA-AS-4.1-ROOM.quote: Room Rent, Boarding, Nursing Expenses as provided by the Hospital/ Nursing Home up to 2% of the sum insured subject to maximum of Rs.5000/- per day. ii. Intensive Care Unit (ICU) / Intensive Cardiac Care Unit (ICCU) expenses up to 5% of sum insured subject to maximum of Rs. 10,000/- per day.
NIVA-AS-4.1-ROOM.source: Arogya Sanjeevani Policy, Niva Bupa Health Insurance Co. Ltd.

NIVA-AS-4.1.1-AMBULANCE.title: Road ambulance capped at Rs 2,000
NIVA-AS-4.1.1-AMBULANCE.quote: Expenses incurred on road Ambulance subject to a maximum of Rs.2000/- per hospitalisation.
NIVA-AS-4.1.1-AMBULANCE.source: Arogya Sanjeevani Policy, Niva Bupa Health Insurance Co. Ltd.

NIVA-AS-6.3-SPECIFIC.title: Specific waiting periods do not apply to accidents
NIVA-AS-6.3-SPECIFIC.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the following listed conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24/36 months of continuous coverage, as may be the case after the date of inception of the first policy with the insurer. This exclusion shall not be applicable for claims arising due to an accident.
NIVA-AS-6.3-SPECIFIC.source: Arogya Sanjeevani Policy, Niva Bupa Health Insurance Co. Ltd.

NIVA-AS-7.6-SPORTS.title: Hazardous sports exclusion applies only to professionals

NIVA-AS-7.6-SPORTS.source: Arogya Sanjeevani Policy, Niva Bupa Health Insurance Co. Ltd.

NIVA-AS-9.5-COPAY.title: 5% co-payment on admissible amount
NIVA-AS-9.5-COPAY.quote: Each and every claim under the Policy shall be subject to a Copayment of 5% applicable to claim amount admissible and payable as per the terms and conditions of the Policy.
NIVA-AS-9.5-COPAY.source: Arogya Sanjeevani Policy, Niva Bupa Health Insurance Co. Ltd.

R-OMBUDSMAN-AFTER-30-DAYS-OR-UNSATISFACT.quote: *(The policyholder may approach the Insurance Ombudsman if his / her complaint is not resolved within 30 days or if the decision of the company is not acceptable to the policyholder.)

R-OMBUDSMAN-BAR-IF-COURT-OR-FORUM-CASE.title: The Ombudsman cannot hear a complaint on the same subject matter that is pending before, or already decided by, a court, consumer forum or arbitrator.
R-OMBUDSMAN-BAR-IF-COURT-OR-FORUM-CASE.quote: No complaint before the Insurance Ombudsman shall be maintainable on the same subject matter on which proceedings are pending before or disposed of by any court or consumer forum or arbitrator.
R-OMBUDSMAN-BAR-IF-COURT-OR-FORUM-CASE.source_detail: Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (as amended up to 09.11.2023; CIO consolidated copy)

R-OMBUDSMAN-CLAIMS-UP-TO-50-LAKH.title: If not satisfied with the insurer's grievance resolution, unresolved or partially resolved complaints can be escalated to the Insurance Ombudsman of the relevant jurisdiction where the claim amount is up to Rs 50 lakh.
R-OMBUDSMAN-CLAIMS-UP-TO-50-LAKH.quote: In case the complainant is not satisfied with the resolution of grievance provided by the insurer, they can escalate the unresolved / partially resolved complaints to Insurance Ombudsman of concerned jurisdiction, in case the claim amount is up to Rs. 50 lakhs.
R-OMBUDSMAN-CLAIMS-UP-TO-50-LAKH.source: IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024
R-OMBUDSMAN-CLAIMS-UP-TO-50-LAKH.source_detail: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024

R-OMBUDSMAN-NO-FEE-FILING-MODES.title: An Ombudsman complaint is free of any charge/fee and can be filed in person, online at cioins.co.in, or in writing by post/email.
R-OMBUDSMAN-NO-FEE-FILING-MODES.quote: The policyholder has option to take up the matter before insurance ombudsman of competent jurisdiction without any charge / fee through any of the following options: a. In person; b. Online by visiting https://cioins.co.in/Complaint/Online; c. In writing through post or through email by giving complete details.
R-OMBUDSMAN-NO-FEE-FILING-MODES.source: IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024
R-OMBUDSMAN-NO-FEE-FILING-MODES.source_detail: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024

R-OMBUDSMAN-ONE-YEAR-LIMIT.title: The Ombudsman complaint must be filed within one year of the insurer's rejection of the representation, of receiving its unsatisfactory decision, or of expiry of one month from sending the representation if no reply was received.
R-OMBUDSMAN-ONE-YEAR-LIMIT.quote: (b) The complaint is made within one year-- (i) after the order of the insurer 1 [or insurance broker, as the case may be,] rejecting the representation is received; or (ii) after receipt of decision of the insurer 1 [or insurance broker, as the case may be], which is not to the satisfaction of the complainant; (iii) after expiry of a period of one month from the date of sending the written representation to the insurer 1 [or insurance broker, as the case may be,] if the insurer or 1 [ insurance broker, as the case may be], named fails to furnish reply to the complainant.
R-OMBUDSMAN-ONE-YEAR-LIMIT.source_detail: Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (as amended up to 09.11.2023; CIO consolidated copy)

R-OMBUDSMAN-PRECONDITION-APPROACH-INSURE.title: Before going to the Ombudsman, the complainant must have made a written/email/online representation to the insurer, and either it was rejected, no reply came within one month of the insurer receiving it, or the reply is unsatisfactory.
R-OMBUDSMAN-PRECONDITION-APPROACH-INSURE.quote: No complaint to the Insurance Ombudsman shall lie unless (a) the complainant 1 [has made a representation in writing or through electronic mail or online through website of the insurer or insurance broker concerned] named in the complaint and-- (i) either the insurer 1 [or insurance broker, as the case may be,] had rejected the complaint; or (ii) the complainant had not received any reply within a period of one month after the insurer 1 [or insurance broker, as the case may be,] received his representation; or (iii) the complainant is not satisfied with the reply given to him by the insurer 1 [or insurance broker, as the case may be.]
R-OMBUDSMAN-PRECONDITION-APPROACH-INSURE.source_detail: Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (as amended up to 09.11.2023; CIO consolidated copy)

R-REJECTION-MUST-CITE-SPECIFIC-CLAUSE.title: Whenever a claim is repudiated, rejected or partly disallowed, the insurer must give full details with reference to the specific terms and conditions of the policy document.
R-REJECTION-MUST-CITE-SPECIFIC-CLAUSE.quote: In case, the claim is repudiated or rejected or disallowed partially, details shall be communicated to the claimant along with full details giving reference to the specific terms and conditions of the policy document.

grievance.subject: Grievance: claim no. CLM-NHI-26-0851877, policy no. NHI/AS/2025/0987765
grievance.body:
Date: 17 September 2026

To
The Grievance Redressal Officer
Nirmaan Health Insurance Co. Ltd.

Subject: Grievance against deductions in claim no. CLM-NHI-26-0851877, policy no. NHI/AS/2025/0987765

Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing about the above claim for the hospitalisation of Arjun Menon at Northstar Ortho & Sports Injury Hospital from 12 August 2026 to 14 August 2026 (Complete tear of anterior cruciate ligament, right knee (sports injury on 02-08-2026)). Your office settled the claim by letter dated 14 August 2026, paying ₹1,72,710 against ₹2,57,300 claimed.

I have checked the decision against the policy wording (Arogya Sanjeevani Policy, Niva Bupa Health Insurance Co. Ltd. (UIN NBHHLIP27056V042627)) and IRDAI's regulations, and I dispute the following:

1. Deduction letter does not cite policy clauses: 1 deduction only says things like "Reasonable & customary charges - surgeon fee restricted to Rs 60,000 as per prevailing rates in the locality". When a claim is partly disallowed, the insurer must refer to the specific terms of the policy. (Ref: IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024: Section 1, Part B, V(3)(iii)(5))

In addition, please give me the basis for the following, with reference to the specific policy terms:

1. Surgeon Fee - Arthroscopic ACL Reconstruction: ₹60,000 deducted as "Reasonable & customary charges - surgeon fee restricted to Rs 60,000 as per prevailing rates in the locality". The policy only pays what other hospitals or doctors in the same area would charge, but your letter gives no comparison or clause. For a network hospital, also ask whether the fee matches the tariff the insurer agreed with that hospital. (Ref: Policy wording: Definition 3.29; IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024: Section 1, Part B, V(3)(iii)(5))

I request you to pay the wrongly deducted ₹0 (about ₹0 after co-payment), and to reply with reasons that refer to the specific terms of the policy. I understand IRDAI requires grievances to be acknowledged immediately and resolved within 14 days. If the grievance is not resolved, I will approach the Insurance Ombudsman under the Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017.

Enclosures: policy schedule, hospital bill, discharge summary, your settlement letter dated 14 August 2026.

Yours faithfully,
Arjun Menon
Policy no. NHI/AS/2025/0987765

Respected Sir/Madam,

1. Complainant: Arjun Menon, policyholder under policy no. NHI/AS/2025/0987765 (Arogya Sanjeevani Policy) issued by Nirmaan Health Insurance Co. Ltd.

2. The claim: hospitalisation of Arjun Menon at Northstar Ortho & Sports Injury Hospital, Bengaluru, from 12 August 2026 to 14 August 2026 for Complete tear of anterior cruciate ligament, right knee (sports injury on 02-08-2026). Amount claimed: ₹2,57,300. Amount paid: ₹1,72,710.

3. The insurer's decision: partial settlement by letter dated 14 August 2026.

4. I first represented to the insurer in writing on [date of your grievance] and [the insurer rejected it on (date) / did not reply within one month / replied on (date) and I am not satisfied]. (Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (as amended up to 09.11.2023; CIO consolidated copy), Rule 14(3)(a) (as amended by G.S.R. 147(E) dated 02.03.2021))

5. Grounds of complaint:

1. Deduction letter does not cite policy clauses: 1 deduction only says things like "Reasonable & customary charges - surgeon fee restricted to Rs 60,000 as per prevailing rates in the locality". When a claim is partly disallowed, the insurer must refer to the specific terms of the policy. (Ref: IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024: Section 1, Part B, V(3)(iii)(5))

6. The insurer has not given the basis for:

1. Surgeon Fee - Arthroscopic ACL Reconstruction: ₹60,000 deducted as "Reasonable & customary charges - surgeon fee restricted to Rs 60,000 as per prevailing rates in the locality". The policy only pays what other hospitals or doctors in the same area would charge, but your letter gives no comparison or clause. For a network hospital, also ask whether the fee matches the tariff the insurer agreed with that hospital. (Ref: Policy wording: Definition 3.29; IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024: Section 1, Part B, V(3)(iii)(5))

Relief sought: direct the insurer to pay ₹0 (the wrongly deducted amount after co-payment) with interest at bank rate + 2% from the date the claim was reported.

I confirm that the same dispute is not pending before, and has not been decided by, any court, consumer forum or arbitrator.

Enclosures: policy schedule and wording, hospital bill, discharge summary, insurer's letter dated 14 August 2026, my grievance and the insurer's reply (if any).

Yours faithfully,
Arjun Menon
